rationale: The only workflow_yaml-editable pattern with met preconditions is dependency caching (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE): package-lock.json exists as a lockfile input and npm/node dependencies are fetched on every run, supported by the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern and the measured batch-hiruni cache experiment. However, each job performs checkout, setup, and dependency installation inside the single composite step pkp/pkp-github-actions@v1, with no separate checkout or install step in the workflow YAML. There is therefore no verifiable point to interpose an actions/cache step keyed on package-lock.json (the lockfile is absent before the composite action runs, and caching after it is useless), so the cache prerequisite cannot be safely satisfied without modifying the composite action, which is out of scope. The schedule-related patterns (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST) are ci_service-scoped and require an approved pause/resume policy or are contraindicated by external dataset dependencies (DATASETS_ACCESS_KEY/dataset_branch); none are established as workflow_yaml changes. No supported optimization preserves coverage while fitting this workflow structure, so no change is made.
